newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil air traffic to grow 8.9 pct this year.
newsitem.headline: Brazil air traffic to grow 8.9 pct this year.

text.p: Airplane traffic is expected to grow 8.9 percent this year in Brazil, partly because airport fees in Brazil are low in comparison with those in many other countries, said airport operator Infraero.

Last year, passenger air transport increased seven percent and air cargo volume jumped 18 percent; 19 new airlines started up operations in Brazil in the last 12 months, including Continental Airlines Inc, Equatoriana de Aviacion and Aerolineas Centrales de Colombia, Infraero said.

Infraero said passenger and airline fees charged at its 67 airports across Brazil were below the international average, with travelers paying only $18 to depart from a Brazilian airport versus $20 at London's Heathrow airport and $23 at Florida's Orlando airport.
A Boeing 747 landing costs $3,227.22 at Sao Paulo's Guarulhos airport, while Germany's Frankfurt airport charges $4,729.32 and Austria's Vienna airport charges $5,269.
Overflying Brazil is also less expensive with every 100 km overflown costing $123.75, while in Germany it costs $266.20 and in neighboring Uruguay it costs $349.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
